scoring_source: supplied task-local descriptions; common predicates inherited from v0.2.4
simulation_adaptations: Canvas bag uses two approximately rectangular panels joined along side folds and a shared-vertex bottom seam, instead of a thin elliptical fan cap. The 20 mouth vertices are uniformly spaced across each lip; rest perimeter matches the requested tier and depth stays 20 cm. A 0.2 mm collision margin supplements the existing 1 mm radius. No hand attachment is added; drawstring, seam thickness and canvas bending still need calibration.

D4 and H8 share the specified drawstring bag: its folded hem is a flexible 4 mm-diameter rim sharing the canvas vertices, with nominal 400 kg/m³ bulk density. The hem retains self, hand, object and table contact; only contact with its own embedded base canvas is excluded. There is no constraint to the hand and the task thresholds are unchanged. Earlier D4 trials omitted this hem and gripped bare canvas.

Canvas bag bending stiffness B=0.0003 N m (MuJoCo elastic2d bend, nominal t=0.001 m, poisson 0.3) is a simulation approximation, not a calibrated canvas. Without it the pressed double layer had no bending model, the opened mouth collapsed into a slit and the pouch pivoted about a single held point. Dimensions, mass, friction, edge constraints and task thresholds are unchanged.
D4 items are staged on the right for one arm to load while the other holds the bag. Upright uses an uncalibrated cap-centroid axis proxy: height >=5 cm, tilt <=30 deg, bottom <=2.5 cm.

Flexible-material edge lengths are monitored at every physics step; extension or compression beyond 10% stops the episode as a numerical/material-model failure. Cloth/bag structural equalities use 2 ms, high-impedance constraints to prevent artificial stretching at small grasp triangles; these are cloth edges, not hand attachments.

Contacts between thin flexible material, the hand/pads, and table use 2 ms stiff contact. A loaded H7 prototype otherwise permitted 10.8 mm pad-shell penetration through a 3 mm board. This resolves collision thickness without increasing friction, motor force limits, or adding attachments; compliance still requires measurement.

Isolated MuJoCo 3.16.0 discrete integrator / Newton solve: implicit elastic and contact stiffness, with unchanged geometry, friction, motor force caps and scoring. CG uses 1000 iterations for articulated shells; independent cloth uses Newton. A 100-iteration CG probe failed to resolve stiff cloth constraints. This is a separately recorded runtime, not a re-evaluation of the frozen 3.10 demonstrations.

Optional grasp-retention assistance: local cloth vertices connect to the contacting robot after positive physical contact. All connections are explicitly released before final success. No prop-prop constraints, teleportation or friction changes. This episode is not a pure-contact or policy benchmark result.
